claims.text: Embedding a low volume fraction of ZrO2 nanoparticles into MnNiSi-based alloys will increase mechanical strength.
Embedding a low volume fraction of ZrO2 nanoparticles into MnNiSi-based alloys will increase toughness.
The nanoparticle addition will not significantly reduce the large magnetocaloric effect.
Powder metallurgy followed by hot isostatic pressing can introduce a controlled low percentage of ZrO2 nanoparticles into the MnNiSi alloy.
Optimized temperature, pressure, and time during hot isostatic pressing will produce a uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
ZrO2 nanoparticles will be uniformly dispersed along grain boundaries and within the microstructure.
Dispersed ZrO2 nanoparticles act as crack deflectors.
Dispersed ZrO2 nanoparticles obstruct dislocation motion.
The nanoparticles impede crack propagation and defect movement, thereby improving toughness and mechanical stability.
ZrO2 is inert with respect to the magnetic exchange interactions in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Because ZrO2 is magnetically inert, the magnetic ordering and phase transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect will remain largely unaltered.
Relative to an unreinforced MnNiSi-based control, the reinforced material will have increased strength and toughness.
Relative to the unreinforced control, the reinforced material will retain a comparable magnetic entropy change.
Keeping nanoparticle content sufficiently low will avoid percolation or clustering and the formation of interfacial phases that interfere with Mn-Ni-Si magnetic exchange.
Excessive or poorly dispersed nanoparticles could create local inhomogeneities and slightly degrade magnetocaloric performance.
